And in the year 427
427 of the Arabs (1035-1036 AD):
Ibn Waththāb the Numayrid, ruler of Harran, gathered a multitude of Kurds and Ma'addites,
and marched against Sibabarak,
which was [held by] the Romans,
and captured it.
And he killed in it three thousand and five hundred people,
and took captive many women and children.
And he came and camped against Edessa,
and cut off provisions from it.
And when the people of Edessa were distressed by famine,
they surrendered the city.
And the Romans fled and fortified themselves in the citadel (phrourion);
and the Arabs attacked the citadel,
and two hundred and fifty men of them were killed.
And when they were not able to capture it,
they plundered the city and departed.
It is said
that the number of boys and girls whom they took captive reached three thousand.
Concerning the beginning of the kingdom of the Seljuks in Persia.
And in this same year, which is the year 1347
1347 of the Greeks (1036 of our Lord):
a people from the Huns who are called Ghuzz, together with the Seljuk amirs, went forth from Hyrcania,
which is the land of the Khazars in the north.
And concerning them, he of holy memory, holy Mar Michael the Patriarch, wrote at length and said:
They are the descendants of Magog, son of Japheth, son of Noah.
And concerning them Ezekiel the prophet prophesied when he said:
Thus says the Lord of lords:
Behold, I am against you, ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal.
And I will gather you and put a bridle in your jaws,
and bring you out of your place,
and all the Persians, Cushites, and Putites with you,
Gomer and all his army, and the house of Togarmah from the recesses of the north.
From early days you were appointed,
and at the end of years you shall come.

in a certain Persian book
which is called the *Mulk-Nāmah*,
saw that its writer says:
From the great and aged amir, old in days, Inanj Beg, I heard him saying:
When Bayghu (or Yabghu) was the Khagan of the Khazars,
a certain warlike amir was in his service,
whose name was Tuqaq,
who was also called Temur-Yaligh,
that is,
'Iron-Bow', on account of his strength.
To him was born a son,
and his name was called Seljuk.
